scientific_hypothesis: A two-cavity Fabry-Perot bandpass filter using Ge (high-index) and ZnS (low-index) dielectric materials, initialized with quarter-wave thicknesses at 4.45 μm center wavelength, will achieve dual-band transmission at 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm with stopband suppression at 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm when thicknesses are computationally optimized within [80, 600] nm bounds.
expected_advantages: Ge/ZnS has high index contrast (~4.0 vs ~2.3) in mid-IR for strong reflectivity
20 layers balances performance with fabrication complexity
Quarter-wave seeding provides physically meaningful initialization
Two cavities enable dual-band or broadened single-band response
known_risks: Material registry may not have Ge or ZnS optical constants in 4-5 μm range
Quarter-wave initialization may not align with dual-band requirement
Thickness tolerance sensitivity increases with layer count
Absorption in Ge may reduce peak transmittance if not properly accounted
expected_observations: best_target_score should rise more slowly than Route 1 due to lower index contrast requiring more precise thickness control
tightest_margin may be lower than Route 1 if stopband depth is insufficient with 12 pairs
valid_candidates should remain high as Si3N4/MgF2 are low-loss dielectrics
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if tightest_margin remains below 0.1 for four consecutive rounds, reduce pair count to 11 and add matching layers at substrate interface
